newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate recovers to 9.6 from 8.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate recovers to 9.6 from 8.6 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate recovered one percentage point to 9.6 percent on Friday, pushed up by stronger volume of term loans.
Demand rose ahead of end-of-week payments and daily trade totalled 62.8 million kuna against the supply of 140 million, dealers said.
Fresh settlements amounted to 53.5 million kuna, half of which were call money at a steady 7.0 percent.
Rates for term loans were 9.0 percent for a three-week borrowing, 11 percent for one-month and 13 percent for two-month loans.
Rates for prolonged one-month loans ranged between 11 and 14 percent.
The kuna midrates for the weekend and Monday eased to 6.5760 from 6.5330 against the dollar and to 3.5650 from 3.5633 versus the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
